conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: I-O status
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 9.1.13.3 "This condition shall not duplicate any condition specified by another I-O status value" -> OK §9.1.13.3 1)); the value is Annex A.1 item 106, OPTIONAL (cite.py --check A.1 "I-O status 0x (value of x). This item is optional" -> OK §A.1 106)). COBOL.NET provides NO '0x' letter status: FileStatusCode defines none and a search of src/Cobol.Net.Runtime for a "0[A-Ma-m]" status literal finds nothing, so the non-duplication constraint is met vacuously and the optional documentation obligation does not arise (docs/CONFORMANCE.md line ~294 records the E.2 item 17 note that only digit '0x' values are reported). Case-equivalence (the NOTE) is moot with no letter value produced. No test: nothing to observe beyond absence. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 85,2002,2014,2023 (E.2 item 17: from 2023 upper/lower-case equivalence is implementor dependent)
rows.rule-text: I-O status = 0x. An implementor-defined condition exists. The value of x is specified by the implementor and may be any of the uppercase letters 'A' through 'M' or lowercase letters 'a' through 'm', where the range of letters is defined by the sequence of Latin letters shown in Table 1, COBOL character repertoire. This condition shall not duplicate any condition specified by another I-O status value. NOTE It is implementor dependent whether or not upper and lower case versions of letters in this context are equivalent.

rows.subject: I-O status
rows.adjudicator-notes: §9.1.13.8 3) '53' when a statement requests a record lock and the run unit holds the implementation maximum (cite.py --check OK §9.1.13.8 3)). RunUnitLockMax = 255 summed over every physical file's RecordLocks (TotalRunUnitLocks), tested after the per-connector ceiling in both LockRecord and PreflightNewLock (the order when both apply is §9.1.13.1 latitude). Probe lock53/lk53.cob (18 connectors on one relative file, LOCK MODE MANUAL MULTIPLE, each READ WITH LOCK on 15 records): connectors 1-17 get 255 locks, connector 18's every READ WITH LOCK -> 53. No spec-derived golden reaches the run-unit ceiling (pb338_read_lock_limit_position reaches only '54'). kb/Work PB707 (open) is about where WRITE/REWRITE preflight returns 53/54 relative to RetryLoop; the behaviour is identical. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002/2014/2023
rows.rule-text: I-O status = 53. The input-output statement is unsuccessful because the statement requested a record lock, but this run unit holds the maximum number of locks allowed by this implementation.

rows.subject: IF directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR1 (cite.py --check 7.3.16.3 OK): '>>IF conditional-expression-1 shall begin on a new line and shall be specified entirely on that line.' Render recognizes a directive only when the TRIMMED line starts with '>>' (begin on a new line; §7.3.3 SR2 allows leading spaces); the cce is exactly the operand of that one line, fragment-parsed by DirectiveExpressionFragment.ParseCce. Probe p16: 'DISPLAY "A" >>IF V = 1' mid-line -> COBOL0307 (rejected). p17: '>>IF V =' with '1' on the next line -> COBOLNET1619 malformed 'V =' (rejected, the cce is not continued onto the next line). Both halves verified. No spec-derived negative test located. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §7.3 compiler-directive facility, incl. conditional compilation, is absent from COBOL-85; the pinned compiler gates >>IF at --std 85 with COBOLNET0900, probe p01)
rows.rule-text: >>IF conditional-expression-1 shall begin on a new line and shall be specified entirely on that line.

rows.subject: IF directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR2 (cite.py --check 7.3.16.3 OK): 'Text-1 shall begin on a new line.' Text written after the cce on the >>IF line is part of the directive operand, and the cce fragment parse rejects it: probe p06 '>>IF V = 1 DISPLAY "A"' -> COBOLNET1619 ">>IF: malformed compile-time expression 'V = 1 DISPLAY "A"'". Text on following lines is text-1 (p01). No spec-derived negative test located. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §7.3 compiler-directive facility, incl. conditional compilation, is absent from COBOL-85; the pinned compiler gates >>IF at --std 85 with COBOLNET0900, probe p01)
rows.rule-text: Text-1 shall begin on a new line.

rows.subject: IF directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR6 (cite.py --check 7.3.16.3 OK): 'Text-1 and text-2 may be any kind of source lines, including compiler directives. Text-1 and text-2 may consist of multiple lines.' Render treats every non-directive line as text (block/omitted) and every directive line in a branch through the same switch with ParentActive frames. Probes: p08 nested >>IF/>>ELSE/>>END-IF and a >>DEFINE inside text-1 (N-TT, Z5 correct); p20 non-COBOL garbage, a missing-copybook COPY and >>SOURCE FORMAT FREE in the omitted text-1, and >>TURN + a multi-line DISPLAY in text-2 -> compiles, prints OK1 OK2. The pb1006 golden derives its expected output from §7.2.1 Step 1 and §7.3.16.4 GR2/GR3 with a directive in the false path. || REFUTED: CONFORMS with test-ref EMPTY. The implementation conforms, but pb1006_source_format_in_false_path does not pin SR6: it pins §7.2.1 Step 1 (SOURCE FORMAT processed in the false path) and §7.3.16.4 GR2/GR3, and every text-1/text-2 in it is a single line, so the 'Text-1 and text-2 may consist of multiple lines' half is never exercised. A golden with multi-line texts carrying nested directives (IF, EVALUATE, DEFINE) in both branches would close the row. — Behaviour conforms and survived attack. Probe t2 put a nested >>EVALUATE, a nested IF/ELSE/END-IF and a >>DEFINE in an omitted multi-line text-1, and a nested EVALUATE with WHEN OTHER, >>PAGE, >>DEFINE, a nested IF and a two-line DISPLAY in an included text-2. The output was exactly G1 G2: the omitted DEFINE took no effect and the included one did. The false path also tolerated an unterminated literal, an invalid column-7 indicator, a continued literal and an incomplete COPY REPLACING (u1-u4). The refutation is the test-ref only. The cited golden is spec-derived, but for a different rule and branch set, and it leaves SR6's multiple-lines half unpinned, so it cannot close this row. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §7.3 compiler-directive facility, incl. conditional compilation, is absent from COBOL-85; the pinned compiler gates >>IF at --std 85 with COBOLNET0900, probe p01)
rows.rule-text: Text-1 and text-2 may be any kind of source lines, including compiler directives. Text-1 and text-2 may consist of multiple lines.

rows.subject: INITIATE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'An INITIATE statement that specifies more than one report-name-1 shall not be specified in an exception checking PERFORM statement.' (cite.py --check 14.9.21.3 -> OK §14.9.21.3 3)). CODE: over region B (imperative-statement-1 + every WHEN / WHEN OTHER / WHEN COMMON body + FINALLY) every descendant InitiateStatementContext with reportName().Length > 1 -> error COBOLNET1605. PROBES s1-s6 (2023): multi-name INITIATE in imperative-statement-1 (s1), a WHEN body (s2), FINALLY (s3), nested inside IF + inline PERFORM (s4), WHEN OTHER / WHEN COMMON (s6) -> COBOLNET1605 each; two single-name INITIATEs (s5) and a multi-name INITIATE AFTER END-PERFORM (s2, s6) accepted and run. The rule counts operands, which is what the check counts. Hygiene only: COBOLNET1605 (and siblings 1606/1607/1612/1613) is a raw string code absent from docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md and DiagnosticCatalog, and it is reported at the PERFORM's position rather than the INITIATE's - see dossier_gaps. No test references COBOLNET1605 - test-needed (negative). [code-location note: B INITIATE check, COBOLNET1605)] || editions as adjudicated: 2023 only (the exception-checking PERFORM, Format 3, is new in 2023 - Annex E 'PERFORM Statement. An exception checking variant of this statement has been added.')
rows.rule-text: An INITIATE statement that specifies more than one report-name-1 shall not be specified in an exception checking PERFORM statement.

rows.subject: INITIATE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: multi-name INITIATE = separate INITIATEs in written order; 'If an implicit INITIATE statement results in the execution of a declarative procedure that executes a RESUME statement with the NEXT STATEMENT phrase, processing resumes at the next implicit INITIATE statement, if any.' (cite.py --check 14.9.21.4 -> OK §14.9.21.4 5)). CODE: BindInitiate binds one BoundInitiate per name inside BoundImplicitSeries.Of (written order), which EcBinder wraps member-by-member. PROBE p2.cob (2023, >>TURN EC-REPORT-ACTIVE EC-REPORT-INACTIVE CHECKING ON, USE AFTER EC-REPORT-ACTIVE ... RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT): `INITIATE R-A.` then `INITIATE R-A R-B.` -> 'HANDLED-A=EC-REPORT-ACTIVE', then R-B IS initiated (the later GENERATE DET-B raises no EC-REPORT-INACTIVE and p2b.rpt holds 'B'), then 'AFTER-MULTI' - processing resumed at the next implicit INITIATE, not at the next statement. p3.cob (--std 85, no checking) same order, R-B initiated. No existing spec-derived test pins sentence 2 for INITIATE (pb1001 uses the multi-name form without an exception) - test-needed. || editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (sentence 1 all editions; sentence 2's RESUME NEXT STATEMENT is reachable only where RESUME / >>TURN exist, 2002+)
rows.rule-text: The results of executing an INITIATE statement in which more than one report-name-1 is specified is the same as if a separate INITIATE statement had been executed for each report-name-1 in the same order as specified in the statement. If an implicit INITIATE statement results in the execution of a declarative procedure that executes a RESUME statement with the NEXT STATEMENT phrase, processing resumes at the next implicit INITIATE statement, if any.
